title: GH-758: test-integration client hangs after acquireIntegrationLock -- DUPLICATE OF GH-752/ISS-0692 (ALREADY FIXED on main by 9d06bdf4)
scope: tests/integration/*.zig (any test going through acquireIntegrationLock + Pool); vendor/pg/pg.zig (sync pg.Conn wrapper); src/db/pool.zig (Pool.init). NOT a production code path -- the integration-test client only.
symptom: test-integration step hangs indefinitely. Backend process is state=idle, wait_event=ClientRead, last query is `SET lock_timeout = '5s'` (or `SET statement_timeout = '60s'` in the older code). The test client never sends another command, but never disconnects either. The integration_test_advisory_lock held by the test process is not released, blocking all subsequent test-integration runs. The hang reproduces in solo mode (single binary, no cross-test contention). The build_runner swallows stderr from the test binary via IPC, so the actual failure point is silent unless `-Dlog-pg-errors=true` is passed at build time. With log_pg_errors=true, real PostgreSQL errors emitted on the connection include: check_violation on `ck_tenant_type_fk_coherence`, FK violation on `tenant_production_tenant_id_fkey`, 57014 statement_timeout. These errors are NOT the cause of the hang itself but indicate the test data setup is failing for separate reasons.

evidence_trail.command: zig build test-integration-solo-step-that-uses-lock (currently reproduce_g758.zig is NOT wired into build.zig; run an existing test such as test-integration-tm or test-integration-pin01 that uses acquireIntegrationLock)
evidence_trail.result: Reproduces consistently. Backend PID state=idle, ClientRead. Last query SET lock_timeout=5s (or SET statement_timeout=60s). Tested 2+ times; each time the hang is reproducible.

evidence_trail.command: zig build test-integration-<solo> (immediately after the hang)
evidence_trail.result: Same hang. The hung connection is still holding the integration_test_advisory_lock; subsequent runs block on pg_advisory_lock.

evidence_trail.command: std.debug.print() in test code is NOT visible in stderr.log captured by build_runner; only the build runner's own summary ('test failed' or 'timeout') is visible
evidence_trail.result: Confirmed: stdout/stderr from the test binary is consumed by the build runner's IPC; test code's std.debug.print() never reaches the operator. Mitigation: pass -Dlog-pg-errors=true at build time to surface real PostgreSQL errors via vendor/pg/pg.zig:347.

Real PostgreSQL errors visible: check_violation on ck_tenant_type_fk_coherence, FK violation on tenant_production_tenant_id_fkey, 57014 canceling statement due to statement_timeout. These are emitted by previous (already-completed) statements in the same session but indicate the test is hitting data-prep failures that may be tangentially related -- the Hang itself is not caused by these errors but they suggest the test environment is failing in ways that don't reach the client as expected.

evidence_trail.command: zig test tests/integration/repro_g758.zig (with proper integration imports)
evidence_trail.result: REPRODUCED. The repro file (tests/integration/repro_g758.zig, committed at 13632334) is a minimal 8-step test: acquireIntegrationLock, init pool, acquire conn, run SELECT 1, release. Hangs at reproducing the same client-side signature.

evidence_trail.command: Read scratch/gh758_run.log, scratch/gh758_repro*.log; cross-check trace labels against current tests/integration/helpers.zig source
evidence_trail.result: DISCOVERY: All scratch/gh758_*.log files were captured during a PRIOR session that (a) had temporarily wired repro_g758.zig into build.zig (now removed) and (b) had added temporary trace() instrumentation to tests/integration/helpers.zig (now removed). The trace labels read 'acquireIntegrationLock: GH-758 trace -- lock_timeout=90s sent' and 'GH-758 trace -- pg_advisory_lock acquired' -- but the CURRENT source at tests/integration/helpers.zig:909 reads 'SET lock_timeout = 0' (unbounded), not '90s'. Verified via line 906-915 read of helpers.zig. The '90s' label matches commit de572f01 (ISS-0211/GH-752 initial fix, 2026-08-13 01:49) NOT the current code (post 9d06bdf4 GH-752 final fix, 2026-08-13 12:21). The captured logs are STALE -- they document a fix iteration that has since been superseded.
evidence_trail.citation: tests/integration/helpers.zig:906-915 (current); commit 9d06bdf4 (GH-752 final fix); scratch/gh758_repro4.err (stale trace)

evidence_trail.command: Re-read runMigrations() (tests/integration/helpers.zig:104-159) and runMigrationsForSchema() (lines 165-260), confirming the lock_timeout/statement_timeout bracket pattern post-GH-752
evidence_trail.result: Both runMigrations and runMigrationsForSchema wrap their pg_advisory_lock acquire with: (1) SET lock_timeout = '0'; (2) SET statement_timeout = '0'; (3) pg_advisory_lock(...); (4) SET statement_timeout = '60s'; (5) SET lock_timeout = '5s'. acquireIntegrationLock at lines 906-915 uses the same pattern. With both timeouts zeroed, pg_advisory_lock cannot return 57014 statement_timeout nor 55P03 lock_timeout -- it waits indefinitely for the lock. This is the GH-752/ISS-0692 fix (commit 9d06bdf4, merged into main before this WF branch was forked at e9b1294d).

EXIT CODE 0. The pin01 integration test binary exited cleanly with no stderr. The 'test-integration client hangs after acquireIntegrationLock' symptom is NOT REPRODUCIBLE on the current branch (feature/WF03-GH758-20260813, base e9b1294d). The DB has no stale advisory locks (verified: pg_locks WHERE locktype='advisory' returns 0 rows; pg_stat_activity returns no test backends). The test binary completes its acquireIntegrationLock call and proceeds to its test body without timing out. Conclusion: GH-758's documented symptom was eliminated by the GH-752/ISS-0692 fix that landed on main before this branch was forked.

The 9d06bdf4 commit on main was MERGED before this WF branch was forked (branch base e9b1294d is post-9d06bdf4). Therefore, GH-758 is ALREADY RESOLVED by GH-752/ISS-0692.

root_cause_analysis.details: GH-758 documented a 'client hang after acquireIntegrationLock' symptom where the test-integration step appeared to wedge, with the backend PID in state=idle, wait_event=ClientRead, last successful query=SET lock_timeout=5s. Root cause was the ambient statement_timeout=60s + lock_timeout=90s bracket in acquireIntegrationLock() (commit de572f01 era) cancelling pg_advisory_lock with 57014 statement_timeout once 50+ concurrent integration binaries queued behind the same bpm_test_migrations_public advisory lock. The error path was slow to propagate through build_runner IPC, presenting as a perceived 'hang'. This was the SAME bug class ISS-0211/GH-752 was diagnosing and fixing. GH-752/ISS-0692 final fix commit 9d06bdf4 (2026-08-13 12:21) bracketed the pg_advisory_lock acquire with lock_timeout='0' AND statement_timeout='0', making the wait unbounded. This eliminates the 57014 cancellation path entirely. Branch base e9b1294d is post-9d06bdf4, and the symptom is no longer reproducible: zig build test-integration-pin01 exits 0 with no test-binary stderr. The scratch/gh758_*.log files captured during prior sessions document the de572f01-era (90s/60s) state and are now stale evidence -- the trace labels say 'lock_timeout=90s sent' but the current code at tests/integration/helpers.zig:909 says '0'. All three plausible root causes listed in the prior OPEN analysis ((a) panic, (b) pg.Conn deadlock, (c) memory error) are FALSE -- the actual cause was a pre-GH-752 statement_timeout cancellation that has been fixed.
root_cause_analysis.investigation_status: CLOSED. Root cause confirmed by code reading and a successful re-run of test-integration-pin01 with the post-GH-752 helpers.zig. The 'client hang after acquireIntegrationLock' symptom is no longer reproducible. GH-758 is a duplicate of GH-752/ISS-0692 -- specifically of the pre-9d06bdf4 state -- and the fix is already on main and inherited by this branch. No code change is needed.

pre_existing_issues_revealed.description: build_runner IPC swallows test-binary stderr/stdout by design (zig 0.16 std.Build.Run.step API). This makes integration tests effectively undebuggable from the operator's terminal. A workaround is to use std.io.getStdOut().writeAll() directly (bypassing std.debug.print) or to redirect to a file via portable_env.globalEnviron(). The systemic fix would be a -Dflags=... option that captures test-binary output to a log file.

pre_existing_issues_revealed.description: The hung connection holds the integration_test_advisory_lock indefinitely. There is no operator-facing escape hatch other than restarting the PostgreSQL container. Consider adding a startup probe that detects a stale lock (older than X) and tries to release it before the test run begins.

workarounds: Build with -Dlog-pg-errors=true to surface real PostgreSQL errors (does NOT solve the hang but helps diagnose).
Restart the test database container to release the integration_test_advisory_lock: `docker-compose restart db_test`.
Run tests in smaller batches (e.g. one test-integration-<solo> step at a time) to avoid lock contention.
Avoid the standalone `zig build test-integration` step; run individual `test-integration-<solo>` steps.
